subtitle: Match Harvey, Faraday, Noether and Meitner to what they discovered, and hear how Lise Meitner missed a Nobel but got an element.

spec.title: Who discovered what? Match four scientists

sources.title: Exercitatio Anatomica de Motu Cordis et Sanguinis in Animalibus
sources.finding: the heart pumps the blood in a continuous circuit round the body

sources.title: Michael Faraday
sources.finding: in 1821 Faraday made a current-carrying wire rotate round a magnet: the first electric motor

sources.title: Noether's theorem
sources.finding: Emmy Noether proved in 1918 that every continuous symmetry of a physical system corresponds to a conserved quantity

commands.speak: William Harvey, an English doctor, showed in 1628 that the heart pumps the same blood round and round the body.
Michael Faraday, a blacksmith's son, built the first electric motor in 1821: a wire that spun round a magnet.
Emmy Noether proved in 1918 that every symmetry in the laws of nature comes with something conserved, such as energy.
Einstein called her a creative mathematical genius.
And Lise Meitner, with her nephew Otto Frisch, explained nuclear fission at the end of 1938: an atom's core splitting in two.
But the Nobel Prize for it went to her colleague Otto Hahn alone.
Science made amends later: element 109 is named meitnerium, after her.
